A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMDocIR study and include appendices A–H. Their text, tables, figures, and equations support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original page/layout retrieval experiments, efficiency measurements, annotation agreement, and a ViDoRe query audit.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a direct-versus-cascade retrieval experiment in Section 5.7 and Table 9.

M1.justification: v3 adds an optional cascade procedure: retrieve pages first, then rank layouts within the selected pages (Section 5.7). This extends v2's direct retrieval procedures. The proposed Phi3 encoders, similarity functions, and contrastive objectives in Appendix C remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten-domain evaluation corpus, seven training subsets, and page/layout tasks. The cascade experiment uses existing coverage. Appendix F retains the ViDoRe query audit; removing its explicit exclusion sentence does not establish a new retrieval evaluation.

E2.justification: New Table 9 expands the evaluated comparison pipelines to same-model cascades and visual-page retrieval followed by ColBERT layout ranking. The original standalone comparator lineup remains unchanged in the main benchmark tables and Appendix A.

E3.justification: Section 5.7 adds top-1/5/10 cascade tests using top-k pages to restrict layout candidates. ColPali's reported per-token dimension changes from 1,024 in v2 Table 13 to 128 in v3 Table 14. Its checkpoint and retained scores are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The new cascade study tests whether page filtering and the choice of second-stage retriever improve layout retrieval. Existing OCR-versus-VLM, image-versus-hybrid, efficiency, and appendix case-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for retrieval results. Annotation agreement and cross-validation reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The pre-existing numerical result tables match. New Table 9 reports Top1/5/10 values of 35.3/58.8/65.4 for Col-Phi3 followed by ColBERT, versus 31.6/54.5/63.3 for direct Col-Phi3; BGE's cascade performs worse than direct BGE. These are newly reported pipeline comparisons, not same-procedure gains across versions.

T1.justification: The formal retrieval definition and Appendix C equations (1)–(6) are unchanged. The expanded explanation of overlap-based recall introduces no new mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the benchmark and dual-task contributions and the claims concerning visual retrieval, training-data usefulness, and VLM-text. The cascade experiment does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 discusses cascade error propagation and connects its benefits to first-stage page recall. Section 5.1 explains why imperfect alignment between MinerU detections and manual labels motivates overlap scoring. Appendix F removes the explicit statement excluding ViDoRe; the dedicated Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies MinerU detections as evaluation inputs, adds bounding-box representation details, names PERF among training techniques, and revises ColPali's documented dimension. It removes the A100 40GB efficiency-test specification and four-A100-80GB training specification. Other checkpoint, training-budget, and resource-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations concerning long-context QA, cross-modal processing, information extraction, efficient training, and synthetic negatives. Section 6 newly identifies MMDocRAG as built upon MMDocIR. These additions broaden context without substantially changing the benchmark's positioning against earlier retrieval datasets.

P1.justification: v3 locally expands layout, annotation, and evaluation explanations, adds the cascade subsection, updates the affiliation, and makes wording edits. Most prose and the overall main-text and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the cascade comparison table and reflows existing tables and text. Figure 2 gains an area-counting clarification. Appendix Figures 8–10 lose red outline boxes while retaining colored layout highlights. The general two-column design and remaining visual content are preserved.

improvement.justification: The cascade comparison provides useful evidence about when page-first retrieval helps or hurts, and Section 5.1 makes layout evaluation easier to interpret. These improve the benchmark's practical usefulness, partly offset by removal of GPU hardware specifications. The gains are limited because the core benchmark and previously reported results remain unchanged.
